READ_THIS_FIRST.instruction_for_ai: DO NOT calculate totals from individual activities. Use the pre-calculated values in 'summary', 'weekly_summary', and 'derived_metrics' sections below. These are already computed accurately from the API data.
READ_THIS_FIRST.display_formatting: For durations and sleep, always display the '_formatted' fields (e.g., sleep_formatted, duration_formatted, total_training_formatted) instead of converting decimal '_hours' values. The formatted fields are pre-calculated from raw seconds and avoid rounding errors.
READ_THIS_FIRST.extended_data_note: ACWR and baselines calculated from 28 days of data
READ_THIS_FIRST.capability_metrics_note: The 'capability' block in derived_metrics contains durability trend (aggregate decoupling 7d/28d), efficiency factor trend (aggregate EF 7d/28d), HRRc trend (heart rate recovery 7d/28d), TID comparison (7d vs 28d distribution drift), power curve delta (MMP shift at anchor durations across 28d windows — energy system adaptation direction), HR curve delta (max sustained HR shift at anchor durations — cardiac adaptation, cross-sport), sustainability profile (per-sport power/HR sustainability table for race estimation — 42d window, sport-filtered), and DFA a1 profile (per-session non-linear HRV index from AlphaHRV Connect IQ field — latest_session + trailing_by_sport with crossing-band LT1/LT2 estimates). These measure HOW the athlete expresses fitness, not just load. Use these for coaching context alongside traditional load metrics. Durability and EF trend direction matters more than absolute values. HRRc is display only — higher = better parasympathetic recovery. Power curve delta rotation_index reveals whether gains are sprint-biased (positive) or endurance-biased (negative). HR curve delta is ambiguous — rising max sustained HR may indicate fitness or fatigue; cross-reference with resting HRV/HR and RPE. Sustainability profile provides race estimation lookup: actual MMP, Coggan predicted (cycling only), CP/W' model (cycling only), model_divergence_pct (actual vs CP — divergence IS the coaching signal). CP/W' is primary for durations ≤20min; Coggan duration factors are the established reference for ≥60min. Source flag (observed_outdoor/observed_indoor) matters for cycling race estimation — indoor MMP is typically 3-5% lower. DFA a1 profile: thresholds (1.0 ≈ LT1, 0.5 ≈ LT2) cycling-validated only — non-cycling sports get rollups but validated=False. Crossing-band estimates: HR is pooled across all sessions; watts are split by environment for cycling (watts_outdoor, watts_indoor with per-environment n_sessions) — compare watts_outdoor against ftp, watts_indoor against ftp_indoor. Non-cycling sports keep pooled watts. Estimates are provisional at confidence='low' (suppressed for calibration delta surfacing) and usable at 'moderate' or 'high'. DFA a1 is a Tier-2 interpretive signal — does NOT enter readiness P0–P3 ladder, does NOT auto-update dossier zones; surfaces calibration deltas only. Quality gate: refuse to interpret when latest_session.sufficient=false or trailing confidence=null. See SECTION_11.md DFA a1 Protocol for full interpretation rules.
READ_THIS_FIRST.readiness_decision_note: The 'readiness_decision' block contains a pre-computed go/modify/skip recommendation with priority level (P0=safety, P1=overload, P2=fatigue, P3=green), individual signal statuses, phase-adjusted thresholds, and structured modification guidance. Use this as the baseline for pre-workout recommendations. Override with explanation in the coach note if the AI's contextual judgment disagrees.

wellness_field_scales.note: All categorical wellness fields use a 1-4 positional scale where 1 = best state, 4 = worst state. Labels differ per field but direction is consistent. Fields are null when not reported.
wellness_field_scales.menstrual: menstrual_phase and menstrual_phase_predicted are not on the 1-4 scale. Values: PERIOD, FOLLICULAR, OVULATION, LUTEAL, etc.

readiness_decision.reason: P3 green light. 6 green, 0 amber (threshold 3), 0 red.

summary.note: Duration calculated from API moving_time field.

derived_metrics.grey_zone_note: Gray Zone % (Z3/tempo) - minimize in polarized training
derived_metrics.quality_intensity_note: Quality Intensity % (Z4+/threshold+) - target ~20% in polarized training
derived_metrics.easy_time_ratio_note: Easy time (Z1+Z2) / Total - target ~80% in polarized training
derived_metrics.hard_days_note: Power ladder: z3+ >= 30min, z4+ >= 10min, z5+ >= 5min, z6+ >= 2min, z7 >= 1min. HR fallback (when no power): z4+ >= 10min, z5+ >= 5min. Per Seiler 3-zone model + Foster. HR-based days flagged with intensity_basis: hr

durability.note: Steady-state power sessions only (VI <= 1.05, VI > 0, >= 60min, power data). Negative decoupling = strong durability. Trend compares 7d vs 28d mean (+/-1% = stable). 28d mean requires >= 5 qualifying sessions; insufficient_sample_28d=true when 1-4 sessions exist (mean suppressed to prevent false alarms).

efficiency_factor.note: Steady-state cycling sessions only (VI <= 1.05, VI > 0, >= 20min, power+HR data). Rising EF = improving aerobic efficiency. Compare like-for-like sessions only — EF varies with intensity. Trend compares 7d vs 28d mean (+/-0.03 = stable).

hrrc.note: HRRc = heart rate recovery (largest 60s HR drop in bpm after exceeding threshold HR for >1 min). Higher = better parasympathetic recovery. Null when threshold not reached, recording stopped before cooldown, or no HR data. Trend: 7d mean vs 28d mean, >10% = meaningful (min 1 session/7d, 3 sessions/28d). Display only — not wired into readiness_decision signals.

tid_comparison.note: Compares 7d vs 28d Seiler TID to detect distribution shifts. pi_delta positive = more polarized acutely.

power_curve_delta.note: Compares MMP at 5 anchor durations (5s neuromuscular, 60s anaerobic, 300s MAP, 1200s threshold, 3600s endurance) across two 28d windows. rotation_index = mean(5s,60s pct_change) - mean(1200s,3600s pct_change). Positive = sprint-biased gains, negative = endurance-biased. 300s excluded from rotation (transitional). Null when either window has fewer than 3 valid anchor durations.

hr_curve_delta.note: Compares max sustained HR at 4 anchor durations (60s anaerobic ceiling, 300s VO2max HR, 1200s threshold HR, 3600s endurance HR) across two 28d windows. rotation_index = mean(60s,300s pct_change) - mean(1200s,3600s pct_change). Positive = intensity-biased HR shift, negative = endurance-biased. No sport filter — HR is cross-sport physiological (dominated by hardest efforts). IMPORTANT: rising max sustained HR is ambiguous — may indicate improved cardiac output (good) or accumulated fatigue/dehydration/heat (bad). Cross-reference with resting HRV, resting HR, RPE, and environmental context before interpreting. Null when either window has fewer than 3 valid anchor durations.

cycling.model_trust_note: CP/W' model (P=CP+W'/t) is primary for durations ≤20min where W' contribution is meaningful. Coggan duration factors (Allen & Coggan, 3rd ed.) are the established reference for ≥60min. 30min is the crossover zone where both apply. model_divergence_pct = (actual - CP_model) / CP_model × 100. Positive divergence at short durations may indicate strong anaerobic capacity or stale W' value. Indoor MMP is typically 3-5% lower than outdoor (cooling, motivation) — source flag indicates which environment produced each anchor.

planned_workouts.name: Tuesday SS-5 4x10 Sweet Spot (FTP 211)
planned_workouts.description:
The week's key session. 4x10 min at 179W (85% of your freshly-minted 211W FTP) with 5 min easy between. HR band 135-148; if you exceed 150 mid-interval, drop 5W. Pass criterion: all four intervals within ~3% of each other. Morning gate: if HRV is still 10%+ below baseline, do only 3 intervals — bail out at the cooldown early.

Warmup
- 10^ Big day. First quality session at FTP 211. The ramp test wrote a check — today we see if the legs cash it. 300^ Warming up properly. Sweet spot without a warm-up is like swimming right after lunch. Technically possible, universally regretted. 660^ Coming up: 4x10 at 179W. That is 6W more than your May intervals. Progress wearing a very small hat.<!> 15m ramp 40-68% 90rpm

- 10^ Two minutes to settle. Breathe. Pick your cadence. Make peace with your saddle.<!> 2m 50% 90rpm
- 10^ Interval 1 of 4. 179W. Settle in like it is a long story you already know the ending of. 300^ Halfway. HR should be cruising 135-148. RPE 7: uncomfortable, but you could still complain in full sentences. 540^ One minute. Hold the watts steady. No victory surges — interval 4 is taking notes.<!> 10m 85% 90rpm
- 10^ Recovery 1. Spin easy at 105W. Shake the legs out. Sip something. 240^ Interval 2 approaches. Same watts, same calm. Boring consistency is the whole assignment.<!> 5m 50% 88rpm
- 10^ Interval 2 of 4. This one usually feels the best of the day. Enjoy it responsibly. 300^ Halfway. Power flat, cadence smooth. You are literally raising your FTP ceiling one steady minute at a time. 540^ Final minute. If HR is over 150, shave 5W. Discipline now buys you interval 4 later.<!> 10m 85% 90rpm
- 10^ Recovery 2. Halfway through the work. The Condor would be proud. It will hear about this on Friday.<!> 5m 50% 88rpm
- 10^ Interval 3 of 4. The honest one. Whatever your legs say here is the truth about FTP 211. 300^ Halfway. Stay on top of the gear. Grinding below 80 rpm turns this into a leg-press class. 540^ One minute. HRV-gate riders: if today was a 3-interval day, you finish at the end of this one with full honors.<!> 10m 85% 90rpm
- 10^ Recovery 3. Deep breaths. One more. The difference between 3x10 and 4x10 is the entire plot of this week.<!> 5m 50% 88rpm
- 10^ Interval 4 of 4. The progression interval. This rep did not exist in May. Make it look routine. 300^ Halfway. Compare: does this feel like interval 1? Within 3% on power = green light to 4x12 next week. 520^ Eighty seconds. Hold form. Smooth to the line — fading now is the only way to fail a passed exam.<!> 10m 85% 90rpm

Cooldown
- 10^ Done. 40 minutes of sweet spot at the new FTP. That was the single biggest deposit of the week. 300^ Spin it all the way down. Recovery starts now: food within the hour, protein included. 560^ Tomorrow is deliberately easy. You earned an evening of being smug about it.<!> 10m ramp 60-40% 85rpm

planned_workouts.name: Wednesday Easy Z2 Spin (60min)
planned_workouts.description:
60 minutes of genuinely easy riding at 116-135W (target ~122W), the day after sweet spot. HR ceiling 124 bpm. This is recovery in disguise — if it feels hard, that is important data, not a challenge.
- 10^ Good morning, sweet spot survivor. Today's intensity setting: decaf. 240^ Legs feel like yesterday happened? Correct. We spin gently and let the adaptation fairies work.<!> 8m ramp 40-55% 90rpm
- 10^ 122W. Lower half of Z2. If your breathing is audible over the fan, you are showing off. Stop it. 480^ HR under 124 today. This hour is where Tuesday's intervals actually become fitness. Hard days tear, easy days build. 900^ Cadence a touch higher today, 90-95. Light gear, fast feet, zero ego. 1320^ Reminder: skipping easy days does not make you tougher. It makes you the person who plateaus in July.<!> 25m 57.9% 92rpm
- 10^ Second half. Even a hair easier. Yes, easier. The plan said so and the plan has lawyers. 420^ Friday the Condor returns from the shop. Two more sleeps. Try to act casual. 780^ Feeling wrecked instead of mellow? Cut to 45 minutes. That is wisdom, not weakness.<!> 17m 56.9% 92rpm
- 10^ Winding down. Tomorrow: 90 minutes of progressive endurance. Today you stored exactly the energy for it. 480^ Done. The most underrated workout of the week, completed. Recovery: nailed.<!> 10m ramp 55-40% 88rpm

planned_workouts.name: Thursday AE-7 Progressive Endurance (90min)
planned_workouts.description:
90 minutes stepping up through Zone 2: 125W, 135W, then 148W. HR ceiling 131 bpm even on the final step — if the last block pushes HR over, hold 140W instead. Gentle durability work: the question is whether your HR stays calm as the watts climb.
- 10^ Thursday: the staircase. Three steps up through Zone 2, each one politely firmer than the last. 300^ This is durability training — teaching your engine to hold power when it would rather negotiate.<!> 10m ramp 45-59% 90rpm
- 10^ Step 1: 25 min at 125W. Conversational. You could narrate a nature documentary right now. 600^ Note your HR here. We will check it against step 3. A small gap = a big aerobic engine. 1200^ Eat something if this is an evening ride. The MDS rule applies indoors too: fuel before you feel it.<!> 25m 59% 90rpm
- 10^ Step 2: 30 min at 135W. The middle child. Slightly harder, still firmly Zone 2. 600^ HR drifting or holding? Holding = your base is setting like good concrete. 1200^ Drink. In October the desert will not offer bidons. Your shed does. Appreciate the shed. 1620^ Three minutes to the final step. It is upper Z2, not a sprint. Adjust expectations accordingly.<!> 30m 64% 90rpm
- 10^ Step 3: 20 min at 148W. Top of Zone 2. The deal: HR stays under 131 or we drop to 140W. No pride, just data. 600^ Halfway. This wattage under control today was your tempo pace last winter. That is what progress looks like. 1020^ Three minutes. Hold it smooth. Tomorrow is rest plus a joyful reunion with a certain bicycle.<!> 20m 70% 90rpm
- 10^ Step down. Indoor week complete: roughly 200 TSS banked before the weekend. 240^ Done. Tomorrow: collect the Condor, check tyres and gears, ride nothing. Saturday you get sky.<!> 5m ramp 65-45% 86rpm

planned_workouts.name: Mon AE-2 Steady Z2 (90min)
planned_workouts.description:
Week 1 of the build to CTL 38-42 by Jul 15. Pure aerobic base - the single most transferable adaptation from Zwift to a 75km trek on tired legs. Target 60-64% FTP (127-135W), cadence 88-95. Ride it boringly well. FTP 211W (Zwift ramp, Jun 3).

Warmup
- 10^ Welcome to the build. Last week you held the line - this week we raise it. +30 TSS, +1 hour, all aerobic. 180^ Easing in. No heroics for 12 minutes - let the engine warm before it works. 480^ Fun fact: your 5-min power jumped 38% over the last 28 days. Base work quietly builds the ceiling everything else lives under.<!> 12m ramp 45-60% 90rpm

- 20^ Settle at ~129W. This should feel like a conversation you could win. 300^ Today HRV sat 20% above your baseline. Green across the board - this is exactly the day to bank volume.<!> 12m 61% 90rpm
- 20^ Nudge to ~131W. Smooth pedal stroke, relaxed shoulders. 420^ On Saturday your long ride decoupled just -0.08%. Translation: zero cardiac drift over 2.5 hours. That is elite durability for a base rider.<!> 15m 62% 91rpm
- 20^ ~133W now. Still Z2. Still talking-pace. The magic of base is that it never feels like the work that it is. 450^ Halfway home. CTL 30 today, climbing toward 38-42 by Jul 15. Every steady minute is a deposit.<!> 15m 63% 91rpm
- 20^ Top of the steady block, ~135W. Hold the form, not just the number. 420^ Weight down from 99kg (May 5) to 95.75 - that is 3.25kg lighter up every climb. The trek thanks you in advance.<!> 15m 64% 92rpm
- 20^ Ease back to ~131W for the run-in. You have done the hard, quiet work.<!> 8m 62% 90rpm

Cooldown
- 10^ Spin it down. Clean finish, no abrupt stops - parasympathetic system, take it from here. 360^ Day 1 of the build banked. ~52 TSS, 90 minutes, all aerobic gold. October is closer than yesterday.<!> 12m ramp 60-42% 88rpm

planned_workouts.name: Tue AE-1 Steady Z2 (75min)
planned_workouts.description:
Midweek aerobic maintenance. Target 60-63% FTP (127-133W), cadence 88-94. Keep HR drift under 5% across the ride - that flat line IS the adaptation. FTP 211W (Zwift ramp, Jun 3).

Warmup
- 10^ Day 2. Yesterday you built, today you stack. Consistency is the only training secret that survives contact with reality. 240^ Ten easy minutes in. Aerobic base needs 4-8 weeks of patience before it pays - you are deep into the bank now.<!> 10m ramp 45-60% 90rpm

- 20^ Settle at ~129W. Nothing flashy. The pros call days like this 'getting the work in' - so do we. 450^ Your efficiency factor is holding at 1.12. Same heart rate, more watts over time = the aerobic engine getting quietly better.<!> 15m 61% 90rpm
- 20^ Up a touch to ~131W. Watch your HR - if it stays flat while watts hold, that is durability in real time. 480^ ACWR sits at 0.91 - dead center of the safe zone. You are loading exactly hard enough to grow and not so hard you break. 840^ Think of every Z2 hour as a mitochondria factory shift. You are hiring fat-burning machinery for the 75km ahead.<!> 18m 62% 91rpm
- 20^ Hold ~131W. Breathe through the nose if you can - a clean sign you are still truly aerobic. 450^ Five rides last week, 5 this week. Two-thirds of the way through today already. Momentum is yours.<!> 15m 62% 91rpm
- 20^ Ease to ~127W for the wind-down. Smooth and tidy to the line.<!> 7m 60% 90rpm

Cooldown
- 10^ Spin it out. Legs loose, mind quiet. 300^ ~44 TSS done. Two days, ~96 TSS banked toward this week's ~314. The trek-fit version of you is being built one boring rep at a time.<!> 10m ramp 60-42% 88rpm

planned_workouts.name: Wed AE-7 Progressive Endurance (90min)
planned_workouts.description_preview:
Three ascending Z2 blocks: 60% -> 65% -> 70% FTP (127W -> 137W -> 148W). Stays aerobic throughout - the step-ups stress durability without tipping into hard work. Watch HR:power across the blocks; small HR creep at the top is normal, a big one means fuel or fatigue. FTP 211W (Zwift ramp, Jun 3).
Warmup
- 10^ Midweek centerpiece. Today the road tilts up gently three times. Each step is small enough to stay aerobic, big enough to matter. 300^ Warming the engine. The genius of progressive endurance: it teaches your body to hold form as the demand rises - exactly the skill of day 4 on the trek.<!> 10m ramp 45-57.9% 90rpm

planned_workouts.name: Thu AE-1 Steady Z2 + Cadence (75min)
planned_workouts.description_preview:
Final weekday ride before Friday rest and the Saturday long ride. Steady 60-63% FTP (127-133W) with two high-cadence (95-100 rpm) spin blocks to keep the legs supple and the session fresh. Easy enough to leave Saturday's tank full. FTP 211W (Zwift ramp, Jun 3).
Warmup
- 10^ Day 4, the last weekday brick. Tomorrow you rest, Saturday you go long. Today: smooth, light, and easy on the legs. 300^ Spinning up. Keep this one honest-easy - its real job is to keep Saturday's 3-hour engine fresh, not to add fatigue.<!> 10m ramp 45-60% 92rpm
